text: {"answerable": false, "answer": "The passages describe how Behler-Parrinello networks handle rotational symmetry, but none of them mention NequIP, so the comparison cannot be made from them. Behler-Parrinello maps coordinates to roto-translationally invariant features, built from radial (distance) and angular (angle) symmetry functions of neighbors, and feeds these into a dense network [W2988055229#031][W3000291311#028]. The passages also describe these symmetry functions as hand-crafted and largely ad hoc, so they require human intervention [W2742127985#002][W2963373387#003]. The input fingerprints are rotation-invariant and carry no directional information, so forces are obtained by differentiating the energy [W2976347420#003]."}
